about: Definition schema of Cosmic Ascension (guideline.md section 7.3, 9.3 Data.Integrity, 10.4).
Authoring time only: nothing here reaches a runtime struct, the hash or a save.

Checked by Tools/cosmic_data_schema.py before Tools/make_data_tables.py touches an asset (python Tools/check_data.py runs the same check without the editor), and by the automation test Cosmic_Ascension.Data.Integrity: this file against the code, the loaded assets against this file.
The checker reads this file first. While it has a problem the data is not looked at.
Every column of a row struct is declared here: a column added to a struct needs its line.
Column kinds (closed list): plain, number, numbers, text, texts, tag, tags, tag_list, tag_map, row, row_map, rows, word_map, enum, conditions, effects, pool, structs
An integer property is declared with integer: true (Data.Integrity holds the columns to the property types).

Row tests (closed list): is, in, gt, ge, lt, le, set, min_len, max_len, each_contains, lacks_type, has_type, has_cond, lacks_cond, slots_in, len_ge_col, pairs_ge_col, ge_col, contains_all, contains_none, zero, lacks_words, no_digits, rows_of

A row rule is 'when -> then' over tests: one column with one test of the list above, 'row' with a row name, 'row_not' with a row name (every other row - B3), 'row_prefix' with one of the table's prefixes (the rows of one kind - B1), or 'none' with a list of tests over the columns of one list of structs (no entry of the list holds every one of them - B4: one choice read as a whole). Each test can be asked of some kinds of column only (the checker holds the table).

What a condition or an effect says of its Tag, its Key and its Value is a closed list in the checker too. A Tag may refuse the tag of the rows of a table that hold tests ('not_tag_of': table, tag column, when) and the tags a condition of the named enumerators reads in any row of any table ('not_read_by') - B4: DelayHazard.
A member of a resource pool (kind pool) is named in a rule as 'Pool.Member' - a member of words.resource, read as a number (B6b [B-6b2c]: a project asks no Causality).

A column of a list of structs (kind structs) is named in a rule as 'List.Column': the test holds when it holds for every entry of the list, and so for an empty list. The tests that name other columns of the row (len_ge_col, pairs_ge_col, ge_col) are not asked of such a column.
A rule added here needs an input that breaks it in Tools/test_data_schema.py: that test walks every rule, unique, pair, target and slot list of this file.
A number range stands here only where the guideline states one. A column without a range is checked for being a finite number.

The keys of this file and the options of each kind are closed lists in the checker, each with the type of its value: a key nothing reads or a value of the wrong type is a problem, so a slip cannot switch a check off.

What a rule names has to exist: a test over a column the table does not declare, a tag the ini lacks, a name that is no enumerator or a row the table neither requires nor has is a problem (it would never hold).
required_rows are the rows the code calls by name: the checker holds them, both ways, to the names in the headers under row_name_sources. A table that has an asset carries must_exist.

epitaph_leaves_out (B5): the DT_Encounters rows whose title the epitaph never shows among a dead vessel's last answers - the code holds the same rows as CosmicRows::EpitaphLeavesOut, so each is a required row of DT_Encounters. A card title that speaks to the reader (a word of words.reader_address, or it ends in a word of words.reader_question_ends) has to be listed there: the death and inauguration pages keep the third person (decision 12-da). The [B-5d1] text audit lists four more, whose titles read as a eulogy under a death (a virtue, a memorial day, the two 'beside' titles of the sacrifice reading - header 3.6-1): those titles stay right on their own cards.

The words of a death (B5 [B-5d1], header 3.5): afterlife_words (an idiom that tells where the dead went, and the words of an afterlife), book_of_life_words (the book of life), called_away_words (a calling read as a death) and remnant_words (the word of election - Log.Record rows only), with death_frame_words (an agent, a sacrifice or a cause of the death - the death row only), rebirth_words (a return or a rebirth - the inauguration rows and Succession. only) and record_object_words (days, names, people or the dead as what was recorded - Log.Record rows only), are matched letter for letter, so a short word is found inside others: they hang on the new places alone - the string keys under Epitaph., Reign., Digest., Succession. and Chronicle. (the two books' chapter), the key Panel.RulerLethal (death_frame_words - B6b [B-6b5]), and the DT_LogTemplates rows of Log.Record with the death and inauguration rows, with the extinction row of DT_Hazards by a row rule (B6b [B-6b5]) - never on a whole column ('잠들지' and '돌아가' already stand elsewhere), save two: the fallen's awareness line (DT_Transcendents.AwarenessTemplates, B6a header 3.2) refuses rebirth_words and called_away_words, a column of its own that only that line fills, and the three text columns of DT_Feats (Title, MythicNarrative, LogTemplates) refuse afterlife_words alone - no feat tells a people's climb as an ascent of the dead (B6b [B-6b5], decision 33).

The words of the awareness and of the end (B6a [B-6a5], header 3.2, 3.4): awareness_words (a sameness, an again and a recognition - the fallen's one second-person line would read as knowing the vessel again; '다시 ' and '알아보았' of rebirth_words let '다시는' and '알아본다' through) hang on DT_Transcendents.AwarenessTemplates alone, and holy_passive (the passive of the holy order and the idiom of an end that comes) on every string key under Chronicle., so that no reason line ties the holy order to the end of a run.

The galaxy laws and the upper rungs (B6b [B-6b2a], header 3.3): a comparison test (gt, ge, lt, le) over a tag map holds when every value of the map holds it - an empty map holds (a galaxy law's spawn factors are at most 1); a conditions column may name the condition types whose Tag it leaves empty ('untagged' - a DT_Feats row's CivHasTreaty: the AI's treaty step signs a non-aggression only); and an effect's Key may say 'not_per_tick' (a per-tick source leaves that Key empty - ChangeReverence's Borders walks the borders where a source is applied once). A condition test names the fields of an entry - type, key and tag, a key or a tag at least, each equal - and lacks_cond holds when no entry of the list has them all (a ruler feat names no selector word of the vessel; no claim card buys the claim time but petition_pressure_measured). rows_of (B6b [B-6b2b]) holds when every row name of a rows column is a row of one of the named tables, each one the column names (the extinction is answered by a project alone - the ark).

The words of the upper rungs (B6b [B-6b5], header 3.3, notes 1.6; decision 33): rung_grasp_words (a rung grasped, reached or raced for, eternity and the order), title_words (a title of election, anointing or a saviour, and the crown), binding_words (the binding, its binder verbs and the shadow - the binding is said in its two story lines alone), triumph_words (a victory, the shadow lifted, mockery, and a link word that makes a deed the price of what follows), stay_words (a ruler who stayed with the dying), self_rescue_words (a people that rescues itself, a new birth and the images of the flood), dawn_words (dawn, light, throne and reign), desolation_words (the quenched lamp, the ceased song, the shut door, the flood, a punishment, the shadow, cold and endurance as merit) and binding_name_words (a tower, a ring, a fence, a binding tool, another work's word or a word of contact or tuning in the name of the binding's work) are matched letter for letter, with holy_passive extended by the end-time idiom. rung_grasp_words and title_words hang on DT_LogTemplates.Templates, DT_Events.LogTemplates, the three template columns of DT_Hazards, DT_Megaprojects.CompleteTemplates and the three text columns of DT_Feats, which also take binding_words, self_rescue_words and triumph_words (no feat binds, rescues itself or buys its rung), and on the string keys Rung., Sight., Chronicle., Epitaph., Digest. and six of the seven keys of the B6b screens (all but Diplomacy.TreatyRungTip); binding_words also hangs on Rung., Chronicle., the three Start. keys and Diplomacy.TreatyRungTip, triumph_words on the three Start. keys, stay_words on Panel.ExtinctionFollows and Panel.RulerLethal, and holy_passive also on Rung.; every list but rung_grasp_words and title_words also hangs on single rows by row rules (the fifth-rung feat, the extinction, the era named after endured pressure, project_binding, and log_far_ascent, log_record_extinct, log_death_extinction and log_fallen_bound), and dawn_words, desolation_words and binding_name_words hang there alone.

The ark's word (B6b [B-6b6], decision 33): ark_words ('방주') stands only in the ark and the fourth-rung feat (project_ark, feat_passage_by_ark) - it hangs on the name and the three template columns of DT_Hazards, on DT_Events.LogTemplates and DT_LogTemplates.Templates, and by two row_not rules on the name and completion lines of every other project and the title, narrative and lines of every other feat; Tools/test_data_schema.py reads every other source for it, ST_CA included. The ark's own row rule keeps rescue, title and holy names out of its name and self-rescue and holy names out of its completion lines, and '노아' is a name of holy_and_myth.

The witness's words (B6b [B-6b8], header 2.8, notes 1.6 rule 7; decision 20): witness_words (a testimony, a record made, a telling or a speaking, and a step back that leaves, looks away or is ashamed - the contracted past forms are listed apart), sign_voice_words (a voice of the sign) and witness_record_words ('기록') hang by one DT_Encounters row rule on the wanderer's cards whose conditions name the claim: witness_words on every text column, sign_voice_words on the body, witness_record_words on every text column but the choices' success lines (a column test cannot tell one choice from another, so the step back's success line is held by the text audit alone). A substring test: a false hit inside a longer word is accepted in this narrow scope. The era of an endured pressure (decision 22) keeps its shape by a DT_Events row rule: the ruled people's condition and the Borders reverence.

The shape words of a people (B7x [B-7x3], header 3.2, notes 5.4 data-3; decision 13): the keys under Shape. - the word the chronicle's fact line and the system panel's people line give a people's present way of life - refuse the lists of Chronicle. with remnant_words and desolation_words, and shape_merit_words ('견디', '남은' - an enduring or a remaining told as a merit), a list that hangs on that prefix alone ('견디' joins no other list: desolation_words also hangs on row rules).

The fenced words of the crossroads (B7x [B-7x4], header 3.5, notes 5.4 data-3): crossroads_words (silence, a fence, a covenant, an ark, a shepherd, a pilgrimage, a sanctuary, the deathless, becoming one) hang with silence_words, by rules alone, on a crossroads card - a DT_Encounters row whose conditions ask CivTimeVectorAtLeast, every text field, with rung_grasp_words and title_words -, on DT_Events.LogTemplates of a row that asks CivTimeVectorAtLeast or BorderingCivHasTrait, and on the scan face log_brick_scan_spread by its row rule. A when has no OR and a log row has no conditions: the brick rows a condition does not reach take row rules in the commit that adds them.
A table whose columns are null has no rows yet: its columns are declared when its first row is written.

rules.why: the leap of a death is drawn between its shortest and its longest: a longest below the shortest is read as the shortest (B5 header decision 3) - a data fault
the rate of the AI's projects multiplies their progress: at 0 or below they would never progress, so the code reads it as 1 with an error line (guideline 4.3, 5.7)

the delay above the third rung multiplies the progress of an AI people's construction of the third rung or above: at 0 or below it would never progress, so the code reads it as 1 with an error line (B6b header 2.6, 3.4, decision 17)

a brick multiplier of a progress or a share multiplies what every tick of a people that carries the brick adds: at 0 or below a settlement or a research would never progress and a hazard would never come, so the code reads such a value as 1 (B7x header section 2.4)
the first life is born into the first life's row, arch_seeker (guideline 5.10)
every immutable law the rules read is listed, and none can be taken out of the list: Law.Hedge keeps the sanctuary (guideline 4.5)
the name pattern of a people drawn for the AI calls its home star (guideline 5.11)
the home of a people drawn for the AI takes a proper name from the galaxy without replacement, never a fixed one two peoples could share (guideline 7.4)
the first life's row is a seeking people no AI people is drawn from: weight 0, its archetype tag, the seeking revelation (guideline 5.10, 5.11)

arch_default is the name bank of last resort for the vessel: a people whose own bank is empty names its vessel from it, and an empty name would leave the death and inauguration lines without their subject (B5 log_death_hazard, log_inauguration, log_inauguration_unnamed - CosmicChronicle::VesselNameOf)

unique.why: at most one selector row per category and revelation mode

rules.why: the calling's own line is told whatever its subject, and no tier window hides it: a line of the calling that waits for a tier is an event row with its sign row (guideline 8.1)
a far line is the same sentence for everyone, told with no subject and no arguments, and the clock of the race stops when a window hides it: log_far_event (guideline 8.1)
a far line is the same sentence for everyone, told with no subject and no arguments, and the clock of the race stops when a window hides it: log_far_ascent (guideline 8.1)
the sign of a claim that joined a sphere is a sign the code tells, about the claimed system and its people: told below the third rung before the fallen's own line (B4 header 2.6, 3.6)
the line of a fleet worn by a higher sphere is the narrator's, with no image of the night's vigil: the vigil is never told as the cause (B4 header 2.7, 3.9)

a record line is a subjectless passive about a place or an event, told by the system's name alone: no role slot, no {PopBand}, no {Civ}, no figure - the two books are no roll of a crowd of people - and no word of an afterlife, the book of life, a calling read as a death or the remnant, nor days, names, people or the dead as what was recorded: the object is a place or an event (B5 header 3.3, 3.5, decision 11-ga)

the death line is the narrator's, in the third person by the vessel's name and the hazard: the calling's line, focused on no system, with no word of an afterlife, the book of life or a calling read as a death, no 'you' across the death, no name of the holy order or its realm, and no agent, sacrifice or cause of the death (B5 header 3.3, 3.6, decision 12-da)

the inauguration line is the narrator's, in the third person by the vessel's name, its people and its system: the calling's line, with no word of an afterlife, the book of life or a calling read as a death, no 'you' across the death, no name of the holy order or its realm, and no word of a return or a rebirth (B5 header 3.3, 3.6, decision 12-da)

the inauguration line of a vessel born in a system a claim joined on the same tick is the narrator's, in the third person by the vessel's name and its people, naming no system - no narrator line about that place follows the fallen's own line (rule 5): the calling's line, with no word of an afterlife, the book of life or a calling read as a death, no 'you' across the death, no name of the holy order or its realm, and no word of a return or a rebirth (B5 header 3.3, 3.6, decision 12-da)

the record of a people that let every system go at an extinction's expiry is a record line, so the record line's rule holds it: {System} alone, no figure, no word of a death, the remnant, nor days, names, people or the dead as what was recorded (B6b header 2.2, 3.3 rule 8, decision 5)

the death line of a ruler at an extinction's expiry is the death line in every way: the narrator's, in the third person by the vessel's name and the hazard, the calling's line, with no word of an afterlife, the book of life or a calling read as a death, no 'you' across the death, no name of the holy order or its realm, no agent, sacrifice or cause of the death, no ruler who stayed with them, and no image of a desolation (B6b header 2.2, 3.3 rules 8 and 13, decision 5; notes 1.6 rule 3)

the line of the binding is told in the actorless passive by the name of the system the work stood on alone: no people and no work is named in it - the people is never the binder - and nothing in it triumphs, lifts the shadow, or lets light or dawn rise over it (B6b header 2.5, 3.3 rules 8 and 13, decision 32; notes 1.6 rule 4)

the nameless variant of log_siege_on_us names no other people: the code chooses it when that people stands far above the ruled one (CosmicKnowing::IsFarAbove), so it says {Civ} and {System} and never {OtherCiv} - the name the map and the scope of telling hide (B6b header 2.9, 3.3 rule 8, decision 19)

the nameless variant of log_treaty_broken names no other people: the code chooses it when that people stands far above the ruled one (CosmicKnowing::IsFarAbove), so it says {Civ} and {Treaty} and never {OtherCiv} - the name the map and the scope of telling hide (B6b header 2.9, 3.3 rule 8, decision 19)

the nameless variant of log_siege_lost names no other people: the code chooses it when that people stands far above the ruled one (CosmicKnowing::IsFarAbove), so it says {Civ} and {System} and never {OtherCiv} - the name the map and the scope of telling hide (B6b header 2.9, 3.3 rule 8, decision 19)

the nameless variant of log_siege_held names no other people: the code chooses it when that people stands far above the ruled one (CosmicKnowing::IsFarAbove), so it says {Civ} and {System} and never {OtherCiv} - the name the map and the scope of telling hide (B6b header 2.9, 3.3 rule 8, decision 19)

the nameless variant of log_siege_lifted names no other people: the code chooses it when that people stands far above the ruled one (CosmicKnowing::IsFarAbove), so it says {Civ} and {System} and never {OtherCiv} - the name the map and the scope of telling hide (B6b header 2.9, 3.3 rule 8, decision 19)

the nameless variant of log_stance_lapsed names no other people: the code chooses it when that people stands far above the ruled one (CosmicKnowing::IsFarAbove), so it says {Civ} and never {OtherCiv} - the name the map and the scope of telling hide (B6b header 2.9, 3.3 rule 8, decision 19)
the scan face of a people spread between the stars tells no rest or silence and none of the fenced words of the crossroads, and is named because a log row has no conditions (B7x header 3.5, S15)

pairs.why: the log category an event category may tell (guideline 8.1)

rules.why: the subject system of a line is the system it names: a Civilization row is about the people alone and names no system, so the name of a system the calling does not know never reaches the feed (guideline 8.1)
a slot row tells with three variants or more (guideline 8.2)
a row fired by name tells with one variant or more (guideline 8.2)

a slot runs for every people: it carries no condition on the vessel, no role effect and no effect on the vessel - the selector words of a slot row that read the vessel are Ruled (B6b header 2.7) and Former of SystemOwnedBy, Former of CivHasNotable and Former of NameNotable (an effect); the other selector words wait for the Phase 4 petitions (guideline 16 #29 (7))
a Lottery row with no weight never fires (guideline 7.5)
only a Lottery row has a weight
a row fired by name has no cooldown key
a sign row is told below MinTierToReveal, so there has to be a tier below it
the calling's own line that waits for a tier comes with its sign row: the viewers below the window hear the sign (guideline 8.1)
a row fired by name is not a slot: the stay condition holds on every tick of its window there (guideline 7.3)

a system-subject row lands on a place and the stay condition is about the people: without a cooldown a Standing row would fire once for every settled system in the one slot, otherwise it lands on whichever settled system comes first (guideline 7.3)

a system-subject row is evaluated on every settled system of its slot, and the bordering condition walks the people's borders on each: it is about the people alone, so it stands on Civilization rows (B7x header section 2.3)
the research stage fires the found row by name: as a slot row it would also fire in the slots (guideline 5.11)
the last-system gate fires the remnant row by name: as a slot row it would also fire in the slots (guideline 4.5)
a death comes only from a hazard's expiry (B5 decision 6): no event row records one (guideline 7.4)
a grace row names no one (guideline 9.3: NameNotable is not carried by Event.Grace rows)
an event row is about a people or one of its settled systems: the system the vessel stands in is a wanderer card's subject (B1)
grace is never drawn by an edict: no grace row waits on an edict the people holds (B2 header :342, B4 header 3.8)
a transcendent's own line is first person: it waits for the third tier, and the viewers below it hear the row's sign (B4 header 3.8 - a door for the rows to come)
the vigil's draw row tells a plain day, with no image of the night's vigil: the vigil is never told as the cause of the easing (B4 header 2.8, 3.9)

an era the people names after its endured pressure is named from its own life and land: no dawn, light, throne or reign, no word of silence, and no desolation, shadow, cold or endurance as merit (B6b header 3.3 / notes 1.6 rule 6; decision 22)

the era of an endured pressure is told for the ruled people alone and raises its neighbours' reverence for the vessel (B6b decision 22, the answer A; header 2.7) - without Ruled every AI people's endurance would lift its neighbours
a line of a people's lived way tells no rest or silence and none of the fenced words of the crossroads (B7x header 3.5, notes 5.4)
a line about a bordering people's brick tells no rest or silence and none of the fenced words of the crossroads (B7x header 3.5, notes 5.4)

unique.why: the universe level labels every galaxy with its name: two rows of one name would read as one galaxy (guideline 5.11, 6.4)
two galaxies never stand on one place - the home holds (0,0), so a row left there has no place yet (guideline 5.11, 7.3)

rules.why: a galaxy other than the home holds no peoples, no brake, no home share and no name pools (guideline 5.11 '고향이 아닌 행의 이 네 값은 0')

unique.why: one transcendent per doctrine in a run (guideline 4.2)

rules.why: the fixed place of the roster belongs to a fallen silence
a transcendent stands on tier 3 or 4 (guideline 4.2: no fallen one on tier 5)
a celestial transcendent has no instance: no sphere, no pressure, no roster weight
the roster of NewGalaxy draws fallen rows only
a fallen one is named by its title, never a name: the spiritual sight's line and tooltip and the log's {Transcendent} slot read it (guideline 4.2, 6.4, 8.2)
a fallen one counterfeits a truth, and its row names that truth: a tag under Truth. (B4 header 3.5, 3.8)
nothing reads a transcendent's voice lines yet: the column stays empty until the code that tells them comes (B4 header 3.5, 3.8)
no transcendent weighs the claim's events: the vigil's draw on Event.Crisis.Claim keeps a factor of 1, so the bound of the theodicy budget the invariant counts holds (B4 header 2.8)
the silent one does not take the words of the revelation it counterfeits nor of the true rest: no 잠잠, 고요, 쉼, 안식 in its own words (B4 header 3.8, 3.9)

a fallen one's claim line speaks to no one: no second person - the player is not called, the holy order and another fallen are not spoken to (B4 header 3.9, the text audit's D1); nor does its lure - the awareness line is the one second person (B6a header 3.2, 3.6)

unique.why: a system holds the tag and the code finds the row by it (guideline 7.3)

rules.why: the claim is placed by the claim rule alone, which holds Law.Remnant (guideline 4.2)
the claim rule places the claim and nothing else (guideline 4.2)
a rebellion is the discontent of a people in its capital, not a draw (guideline 4.1)
a Draw row is drawn every tick: a chance of 0 is a slip, and a hazard that only an effect or a hook places will have a spawn rule of its own (guideline 7.3, Phase 4)
only a drawn hazard has a chance: the capital rule and the claim rule draw nothing (guideline 7.4)
a branch is a chance and the effects it takes instead (guideline 4.1)
branch effects without a chance are never applied (guideline 4.1)
a death comes only from a hazard's own expiry, on its own side (B5 decision 6-ga, header 3.5): never from its branch, the damage to its neighbours or its resolution (guideline 7.4)
the fallen cannot touch a life - the claim takes from the living only - and the visitation is the holy order's own: no claim, visitation or cult kills (B5 header 3.5)

a hazard a fallen one's doctrine brings never kills at its expiry, whatever its tag: the fallen cannot touch a life, so a row with a SourceDoctrine carries no death (B5 header 3.5; the one death decision 6-ga opens is no doctrine's)

the supernova precursor's expiry destroys the system, and the death line mourns a star that stays: no death at its expiry until it has a death row of its own (B5 header 8 [B-5d2], DECISIONS_LOG [B-5d1] (11))

the extinction's loss is the expiry's code - its people lets every system go and its ruler dies (CosmicHazards::LetPeopleGo, KillsTheRulerOf): its row carries no expiry effect of its own, no branch and no damage to the neighbours, and it is answered by a project alone - the ark (B6b header 2.2, 3.3 rule 5, decision 5)

the extinction's lines tell a loss and end in mourning: no ruler who stayed, no agent, sacrifice or cause of a death, no image of a desolation, a flood, a punishment or the claimant's shadow, and its resolution rescues no one (B6b header 3.3 / notes 1.6 rule 3; decision 33)
the leader of a cult has no name (guideline 4.1)
the stage reads the spawn conditions on every tick, and the stay condition holds on every tick of its window, not in one slot (guideline 7.3)
the stage reads the spawn conditions of every Draw row on every settled system on every tick: the bordering condition would walk the owner's borders once a system and a tick (B7x header section 2.3)
only stage code behind the last-system gate takes a system: an expiry hands nothing over, and neither does a resolution, which an expiry may run on a neighbour (guideline 4.5, 16 #53 (1))
a resolution or an expiry does not resolve again on its own system: a row that resolves what it places would never end (guideline 7.3)
a project asks no Causality: no people earns any (its income is 0 - guideline 16 #90), so a project that asks it would never be paid and its slot would stand for good (B6b header 3.3 rule 7)

the binding's work is named and told as the people's plain work: its name has no tower, ring, fence, binding tool, contact or tuning word and no word another work owns, and its completion line neither binds, triumphs, nor lets light or dawn rise over the shadow (B6b header 3.3 / notes 1.6 rule 4; decision 32; header rule 14)

the people crosses the extinction in the ark it built; the ark is no one's rescuer - no rescue, title or holy name in its name, no self-rescue, new birth, washing, new land or Flood picture in its completion lines (B6b header 3.3 rule 13, 3.5 rule 2, decision 33)
'방주' is the ark's word: no other project is named or told with it - it stands only in the ark and the fourth-rung feat (B6b decision 33)
the wanderer's feats are judged from Phase 4, with their first row: until then no row walks that path (guideline 3.2, 7.5)
a feat lifts its people one rung: from the first to the second (guideline 3.2; the judgment does not judge another row)
a feat lifts its people one rung: from the second to the third (guideline 3.2; the judgment does not judge another row)
a feat lifts its people one rung: from the third to the fourth (guideline 3.2; the judgment does not judge another row)
a feat lifts its people one rung: from the fourth to the fifth (guideline 3.2; the judgment does not judge another row)
the fifth rung is the last: no feat climbs from it (guideline 3.2)
no people climbs without a deed: a feat holds one condition or more (guideline 3.2; the judgment does not judge a row without one)

a ruler feat row judges every people, the AI's too (guideline 4.3): its conditions do not read the vessel, and its price records no role effect and touches no vessel (a death comes only from a hazard's expiry - B5 decision 6). The rungs stand apart: no ruler row reads the vessel (guideline 16 #1 closed - B6b answer A3); a wanderer's feat is judged on the vessel and gets its own rules with its first row (guideline 16 #28)
a feat's price records no death on any path, the wanderer's too when its rows come: a death comes only from a hazard's own expiry (B5 decision 6-ga, header 3.5)

a ruler row never reads a sealed transcendent: an AI is judged from tick 0, so another people's binding would lift it for nothing - the binding is read by MegaprojectComplete of the people that made it (B6b decision 12, guideline 16 #73)

a ruler row names no selector word of the vessel either: Ruled and Former of SystemOwnedBy and Former of CivHasNotable in its conditions, and Former of NameNotable in its price (every people's climb pays it, an AI's too), resolve from the vessel (the people it rules, the one it left), so the row would judge the ruled people apart from every AI or name a notable in the vessel's former people (B6b answer A3, header 3.3 rule 6)

the fifth rung is a place the people came to stand on, not one it reached or was handed: its feat row's title, narrative and lines carry no passive of the holy order or end-time idiom, and no gold, light, dawn or reign (B6b header 3.3 / notes 1.6 rule 1; decisions 26 and 33)
'방주' is said among the feats by the fourth-rung feat alone, whose deed is the ark: no other feat's title, narrative or lines carry it (B6b decision 33)
K4 - a rung comes from a feat's deed, never from a brick or a mutation (B7x header K4)
a petition's words name no holy word, no soul verb and no rescue word in any field: the name of no god, the faith's gestures in the elders' voice alone (B4 header 3.8, 3.9; MVP item 2)
a card is put before a role: every row carries the condition PlayerRoleIs (guideline 5.10, B1)
a petition is put before a ruler and is about the ruled people or one of its settled systems (guideline 5.10, B1)

a ruler's card does not wait on the vessel's own rung: the ruler's personal rung never rises (B6a header 1.1, 3.1, decision 9), so a PlayerTierAtLeast of 2 or more on a row put before a ruler never holds and its card never comes - petition_exalt waited on it from [A-2b] to [B-6a6] and now reads the ruled people's rung (CivTierAtLeast). PlayerTierAtLeast 1 always holds, so the enumerator is kept off such a row entirely. The block that raises the personal rung (guideline 16 #1, #141) lifts this rule
a wanderer's card is put before a wanderer, about the system the vessel stands in, and checks the vessel: a people's Stability is not the wanderer's (B1)
an arrival card can come on a system no people owns: its texts name the system alone (B1)

a card records no death (B5: a death comes only from a hazard's expiry; a card's lethality is 16 #151) and runs no per-tick effect; the effects that grant, place, take or name wait for the rows that use them (guideline 5.10, 7.4)
the subject system of a card is the system it names: a Civilization row is about the people alone and names no system (guideline 8.1)

only the first contact card is about another people (B3 header section 2.9): the answer gives SetStance its people and fills {OtherCiv} for that card alone - on any other a stance would fall on no one, the name would be empty words, and a wanderer's card would set an AI people's stance (section 2.8)
the first meeting puts the first contact card by name, about the ruled people: as a Standing or Lottery row it would come on its own - at the first tick of every reign (B3 header section 2.9)
a row the knowing stage puts is picked by its weight among the rows of its moment (guideline 5.10)
a row put by name (the next card of a chain) is never picked: it has no weight
a card without voices speaks through its Body
a voiced card speaks through its two voices, the council's and the elders' of the congregation, and its Body stays empty (guideline 5.10)
an edict and a fleet are the ruler's: EnactEdict and DelayHazard stand in a petition's answer, never in a wanderer's card (B4 header 2.2, 3.8)
the gate of a choice reads its OnSuccess alone (CosmicPetitions::ChoiceGateOf): an edict or a delay in OnFailure would stand behind no gate (B4 header 2.4, 3.8)
a choice that enacts an edict or buys time is not rolled for: the gate stands before the answer's draw, and a roll would hang the edict or the fleet on Stability (B4 header 2.4, 3.3, 3.8)
the edict's own EnactCost is the one price of the choice that enacts it: that choice asks nothing more (B4 header 3.8)

a card is never blocked: with one waiting place a card whose every choice is gated would block every card behind it, so a card with a gated choice (SetStance, EnactEdict, DelayHazard) holds a choice with no cost and no gate - said the other way round: a card without such a choice carries no gate (B4 header 2.4, 3.8)
a card on the claim does not end it: a row whose conditions name the claim carries no ResolveHazard, so the theodicy's count of the claims stays as it is (B6b header 2.8, 3.3 rule 8')

nor does any card, whatever its conditions: no answer resolves the claim, nor an untagged hazard (which ends whatever hazard stands - the claim too, on a card whose conditions name no hazard or an untagged one); the theodicy's count reads the claims of DT_Events alone, so this is the cards' side of rule 8' (B6b header 2.8, 3.3 rule 8')

the claim's time is bought by one card alone, the fleet of petition_pressure_measured: one card more of 50 ticks would break the theodicy's bound the Data.Integrity invariant keeps (B6b header 2.8, 3.3 rule 8')

a wanderer's card on the claim is a sign seen or measured: it does not testify, record, tell or speak, the sign has no voice, and the step back neither leaves nor shames (B6b header 2.8, notes 1.6 rule 7; decision 20). A substring test: the contracted past forms are listed apart, and a false hit inside a longer word is accepted within this narrow scope

a crossroads card tells what a people did and where it then stands: its words name no rest or silence, no grasp of a rung, no title, and none of the fenced words of the crossroads - silence, fence, covenant, ark, shepherd, pilgrimage, sanctuary, the deathless, becoming one (B7x header 3.5, notes 5.4)
a held edict multiplies the fleet's growth: at 0 the inherited edict would keep the ruler's fleet at 0 from the first tick, so the code reads a factor that is not above 0 as 1 (B3 header 3.2)
a held edict damps the pressure's drain on Stability, never undoes it: a factor in (0, 1], and the code reads a factor that is not above 0 as 1 (B4 header 2.3)

a galaxy law is an edict of the fourth rung whose two hazard hooks reach every settled system of the holder's galaxy: it only shields - a spawn factor at most 1 (its countdown bonus is at least 0 on every row) - and has no hook on the claim (the theodicy's bound W stays), on the extinction or on the supernova's warning (no other people's feat is held back), and no hazard row lists it as an answer (Data.Integrity) (B6b header 2.4, decision 9)
